answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a scarce-slot auction mechanism. Each identity must secure a bid for a limited slot, starting at 10 tokens, with the price climbing by 5 tokens for every additional bidder. A farm aiming to create five fake accounts faces escalating costs of up to 50 tokens within a single epoch due to the need for unrelated sponsors. This economic model functions like a lagoon that only a few boats can harbor; those trying to flood it with multiple bids will quickly find their resources drained like nectar in a dry season.
